sentence_stem: If only I had studied harder,
correct_completion: I would have passed the exam.
full_sentence: If only I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
acceptable_variants: I would have got a higher score.
I would have done much better.

options.text: I will pass the exam tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: The future tense does not express regret about a past action that did not happen.

options.text: I would have passed the exam.
I passed the exam last week.
options.why_wrong: The simple past reports a real past event and does not express regret about an unreal situation.

options.text: I would pass the exam easily.
options.why_wrong: The present conditional refers to the present or future, not to a past result that did not happen.

grammar_focus: Third conditional with 'if only' to express past regret
explanation: 'If only' followed by the past perfect expresses regret about a past situation that did not happen, so the main clause needs 'would have' plus the past participle. Ukrainian speakers may find this structure tricky because Ukrainian uses past-tense forms with a conditional particle for all unreal situations, so the English pattern is built differently.
translation: Якби я лише більше вчився, я б склав іспит.
